paper.title: Neural Combinatorial Clustered Bandits for Recommendation Systems

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial bandit with semi-bandit feedback and neural reward models
unmapped: N base arms, super arms are all subsets of size K (paper's N is number of base arms, K super-arm size)

Unknown base-arm reward function h(x) in [0,1] learned by an overparameterized ReLU network (NTK regime); unknown monotone Lipschitz super-arm reward u(S,h) learned by a monotone neural network; no oracle
Context sequence not specified as stochastic; contexts change across rounds
settings.definition_quote: At the start of every round t, the agent observes the context vectors of all arms ... and chooses a subset of the available arms, namely a super arm S_t \subset [N] with a fixed size, or budget, K ... r_{t,i} = h(x_{t,i}) + \xi_{t,i} ... where h is an unknown function satisfying 0 \leq h(x) \leq 1 and \xi_{t,i} is \zeta-sub-Gaussian noise

symbols.d_tilde: effective dimension of the NTK matrix H with regularization lambda_1: log det(I + H/lambda_1)/log(1+TN/lambda_1)

conditions: Assumption 1: h Lipschitz in context (constant B')
Assumption 2: u Lipschitz in base-arm means (constant B)
Assumption 4: ||x||_2 = 1, symmetric context entries, NTK H >= lambda_0 I
Assumption 5: clustering assumption with decreasing delta_t (proof takes delta_t = C_5/t) and non-decreasing P_t
Assumption 6: mean cluster contexts have no zero entries
tuning: C_2 L K <= lambda_1 <= 16 m 81 T^{-2 beta alpha+1} K^2 n^{2L_m} / e_T^2
J = 2 log(sqrt(lambda_1/(TK))/(lambda_1 + C_3 T K L)) T K L/(C_1 lambda_1)

source.label: thm_1
source.quote: Supposing that Assumptions 1-6 hold, let h=[h(x^i)]_{i=1}^{TN}, and select the hyperparameters ... Then if m is chosen such that it satisfies Condition 1, the cumulative expected regret of NeUClust over T rounds is bounded by \mathcal{R}(T) = \widetilde{O}(\widetilde{d}\sqrt{T})

results.notes: Regret defined as sum of u(S_t*,h) - u(S_t,h) without explicit expectation; paper calls it 'cumulative expected regret' but the proof relies on high-probability events (1-Delta) from lemmas, so recorded as high-probability / regret_unspecified quantity ambiguity. Full explicit bound in appendix contains K, K^2, N, sqrt(d), n^{L_m} factors hidden in O-tilde. Appendix restates as Theorem 2 (same result).
